title: Polling done carefully
description:
Before webhooks, write the poller lesson 4.01 describes, including its awkward edge case.

```python
class Poller:
    def __init__(self, fetch, min_interval=5, max_interval=300): ...
    def poll(self): ...          # -> list of new or changed items
    since                        # the checkpoint
    interval                     # seconds until the next poll
```

`fetch(since)` returns every item whose `updated_at` is **greater than or equal to** `since` (all items when `since` is `None`). Each item is a dict with an `id` and an integer `updated_at`.

**poll()** calls `fetch(self.since)` and returns, in the order fetched, the items that are new or changed since the last poll:

- An item whose `updated_at` is **greater** than the checkpoint is always returned.
- An item whose `updated_at` **equals** the checkpoint is returned only if its `id` was not already seen at that timestamp. (With `>=`, the API sends back items you already have.)
- Afterwards the checkpoint `since` becomes the largest `updated_at` fetched, if that is larger, and the ids seen at the checkpoint timestamp are remembered (all of them: those from earlier polls at the same timestamp as well).

**interval** starts at `min_interval`. After a poll that returned something, it halves, but not below `min_interval`; after a poll that returned nothing, it doubles, but not above `max_interval`.
hints: Remember two things between polls: the checkpoint, and the set of ids already seen **at** that checkpoint timestamp. When the checkpoint moves forward, start the set again.
An empty first poll leaves the checkpoint at `None`: there is nothing to move it to yet.
unitTests:
class Api:
    def __init__(self):
        self.items = {}
        self.asked = []
    def put(self, id, updated_at):
        self.items[id] = {"id": id, "updated_at": updated_at}
    def __call__(self, since):
        self.asked.append(since)
        found = [i for i in self.items.values() if since is None or i["updated_at"] >= since]
        return sorted(found, key=lambda i: (i["updated_at"], i["id"]))

@test("the first poll returns everything")
def _():
    api = Api()
    api.put("a", 10); api.put("b", 12)
    p = Poller(api)
    check_eq([i["id"] for i in p.poll()], ["a", "b"])
    check_eq(p.since, 12)
    check_eq(api.asked, [None])

@test("items at the checkpoint are not repeated")
def _():
    api = Api()
    api.put("a", 10); api.put("b", 10)
    p = Poller(api)
    p.poll()
    check_eq(p.poll(), [])
    api.put("c", 10)
    check_eq([i["id"] for i in p.poll()], ["c"])
    check_eq(p.poll(), [])
    check_eq(api.asked, [None, 10, 10, 10])

@test("an item changed again later")
def _():
    api = Api()
    api.put("a", 10); api.put("b", 10)
    p = Poller(api)
    p.poll()
    api.put("a", 15)
    got = p.poll()
    check_eq(got, [{"id": "a", "updated_at": 15}])
    check_eq(p.since, 15)
    api.put("b", 15)
    check_eq(p.poll(), [{"id": "b", "updated_at": 15}])
    check_eq(p.poll(), [])

@test("the interval adapts")
def _():
    api = Api()
    p = Poller(api, min_interval=5, max_interval=40)
    intervals = []
    for _ in range(5):
        p.poll()
        intervals.append(p.interval)
    check_eq(intervals, [10, 20, 40, 40, 40])
    api.put("x", 1)
    p.poll()
    check_eq(p.interval, 20)
    api.put("y", 2)
    p.poll()
    api.put("z", 3)
    p.poll()
    api.put("w", 4)
    p.poll()
    check_eq(p.interval, 5)
